title: Route Density Trades — Pest Control, Pool Service, and Window Washing
content:
###  **Profit Lives in the Drive Time** 

For recurring service businesses, revenue per customer is largely fixed. What varies is how many customers a technician can serve in a day — and that depends almost entirely on how far apart they are. 

Ten customers on adjacent streets are worth substantially more than twenty spread across a county. 

###  **Why Growth Can Reduce Margin** 

A pest control company that adds customers wherever they come from will grow revenue while margin quietly erodes, because each scattered account adds drive time that produces nothing. 

This is one of the few situations where more customers can genuinely make a business worse. 

###  **The Problem With Most Lead Sources** 

Paid leads arrive from wherever the algorithm finds them. There is no way to request customers on a specific street, and no way to concentrate growth where routes already run. 

###  **What Territory-Based Outreach Changes** 

Field outreach is inherently geographic. Coverage happens street by street, which means growth compounds in exactly the areas chosen, rather than scattering. 

###  **Trades That Depend on This** 

Pest control, pool cleaning, lawn care, window washing, gutter cleaning, and duct cleaning all share the same economics: the value of a new customer depends heavily on who else you already serve nearby.
